Internal helper: group sizes and within-group variation of an outcome

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_group_shape.Rd

What jt() and jaov() need to know before they compute anything: how many analysis cases each group holds, and whether the outcome varies inside it. A group of one case has no variance, and a group whose cases all hold one value has a variance of zero; R answers both in its own words ("not enough 'y' observations", "data are essentially constant"), or with an F of 27815876027865139260134097158144 (Session 346).

Usage

.jst_group_shape(y, g)

Arguments

y

Numeric vector; the outcome.

g

Factor; the groups, with no empty level.

Value

A list: n (cases per group, named by level), flat (logical per group: two or more cases, all holding one value), mean and var (per group; var is NA for a group of one case).
